title: QBR - Keystone Fintech Health Check
next_steps: Redwood to send updated pricing & usage breakdown by 2026-10-01
Customer to share 1 week sample traffic + schema (s3 csv) by 2026-10-04
Schedule technical benchmark with staging cluster week of 2026-10-11
action_items: Maya Chen - Share cost optimization suggestions (batching + quantization profiles) - 2026-10-01
Samir Shah - Set up staging endpoint and run 1k-request benchmark - 2026-10-12
Marcus Lee - Provide anonymized traffic sample and current token distribution - 2026-10-04
summary: Quarterly business review covering usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer interested in cost optimizations (dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs), tighter SLOs, and a short pilot for quantized models in staging.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give it a few sec for folks to pop in. Uh, quick agenda: usage, cost, reliability, roadmap and next steps.
00:18 Olivia Grant: Sounds good. We, we have the VP of product, Olivia here. Marcus from MLOps and Priya from eng as well.
00:25 Diego Rivera: Hey Olivia, great to see you — Diego here, I'm the AE, Samir is our SE.
00:30 Samir Shah: hey all, hi.
00:36 Olivia Grant: Quick note, we're recording this internally as well.
00:40 Maya Chen: Great, thanks. First slide, usage trends. Marcus can you confirm the main workloads — customer support generation and document embeddings?
00:52 Marcus Lee: Yeah, primary is conversational support (response gen) with some embeddings for retrieval. Peak qps around 40 req/s, average token generation per request about 240 tokens. There's a long tail of 2k token docs for embeddings.
01:08 Maya Chen: Got it. From Redwood's side, we see monthly token volume up 28% quarter over quarter, embeddings stable. Your unit costs have increased primarily due to longer sequences and retries — looks like a retry storm on the 9th because of transient timeouts.
01:28 Priya Nair: Yeah we saw that. That was during a deploy where our downstream cache had a problem, so we retried client side. We fixed it but want to look at retry budget/SLAs.
01:40 Samir Shah: On the retry side, we can implement idempotency keys and more conservative retry backoffs; we also have request-level tracing turned on for you so we can pull the traces.
01:50 Marcus Lee: That would help. Can you share traces or the sample logs?
01:55 Diego Rivera: I'll drop the traces link after the call. (link: https://redwood.app/keystone/traces/09-09)
02:02 Olivia Grant: Cool. On cost, the finance team called out an increase in unit cost month over month, group CFO wondering if dedicated capacity makes sense.
02:12 Maya Chen: Totally. This is a common question — dedicated often reduces per-token costs if you have predictable sustained volume, but it requires commit and has capacity planning considerations. We should compare estimated committed spend vs current hosted spend net of savings from batching and quantization.
02:29 Marcus Lee: We're particularly sensitive to P95 latency for live chat, target under 300ms end-to-end for short prompts.
02:36 Samir Shah: For P95 sub-300ms we recommend a small dedicated pool with pre-warmed KV cache and prefix caching; latency gains are from avoiding cold starts and running optimized kernels. But quantization can add variability — it's usually fine but depends on model.
02:51 Priya Nair: Question: are there SOC2 / ISO controls if we move dedicated within our VPC? We need audit logs and KMS integration.
03:00 Maya Chen: Yes — for Redwood Dedicated and Private, we provide KMS integration, SAML SSO, RBAC and audit logs. We have a SOC 2 report and ISO certs in the security pack. I'll share the security docs. (doc: https://redwood.in/security/soc2.pdf)
03:14 Olivia Grant: Great. Also compliance asked about data residency — some EU traffic should stay in eu-west.
03:20 Diego Rivera: We can route by region, you can pin routes to eu-west instances; Redwood routing policy supports region pinning + fallbacks.
03:28 Marcus Lee: Perfect.
03:30 Maya Chen: On reliability, you mentioned two incidents last month — we tracked them as transient GPU OOM and a model rollout mismatch. Can we quickly go over root causes?
03:40 Priya Nair: The OOM was on a batch in production when we had a very long prompt; our client didn't enforce max_length.
03:48 Samir Shah: We flagged that on our side — setting a strict client-side token limit and enabling per-request max_seq will avoid it. We can also enable server-side request validation to reject too-large requests and surface a clear error.
04:00 Marcus Lee: OK. For the model rollout mismatch, can you remind us what happened?
04:04 Diego Rivera: There was a canary rollout that didn't correctly fallback to the previous quantized variant, so some requests hit an incompatible compile which increased latency. We're putting additional checks into the rollout pipeline: architecture compatibility matrix and automatic fallback.
04:20 Olivia Grant: Does Redwood support automatic rollback policies?
04:23 Samir Shah: Yes — canary with automatic rollback on latency or error-rate anomalies. We can tune thresholds to your tolerance.
04:31 Maya Chen: Moving to cost optimization — Samir, you had suggestions?
04:34 Samir Shah: Sure — short list: 1) enable automatic prefix/KV caching for common prompts; 2) tune batching window to balance latency and throughput; 3) try int8 quantized model for background/async workloads; 4) use dedicated for steady daytime traffic and hosted for spikes.
04:52 Priya Nair: For quantization, what's the expected degradation in quality? We can't have bad hallucinations for legal doc summaries.
04:58 Samir Shah: For most transformer-based models, int8 causes negligible quality drop for summarization-like tasks; we recommend running a small eval suite (we can run your prompts vs baseline) to quantify.
05:10 Marcus Lee: We'll need to set up that eval. Priya, can you pull the prompt sets?
05:14 Priya Nair: Yeah, I can get that to you by end of week.
05:17 Maya Chen: Great — that feeds into next step: run a quantized pilot in staging.
05:22 Olivia Grant: Timeline wise, finance wants conclusions within 30 days to decide on Dedicated commit for Q4.
05:28 Diego Rivera: Understood. We can aim to have pilot results and updated TCO by Oct 8.
05:33 Maya Chen: I'll own the TCO: we'll send a comparison spreadsheet with assumptions (batch sizes, p95 latency targets, commit levels).
05:40 Olivia Grant: Thanks.
05:42 Samir Shah: On the technical benchmark — we'll run three profiles: live chat short prompts (<=300 tokens), long document summarize (1-2k tokens), and embeddings bulk (batching). We'll measure P50/P95, throughput and cost per 1k tokens.
06:00 Marcus Lee: For embeddings we care about cost per vector and latency for batch indexing. We typically do bulk offline jobs overnight.
06:07 Samir Shah: Bulk jobs should be quantized and batched heavily; you can use Redwood Optimize suggestions to set batch size.
06:14 Priya Nair: Any immediate configuration changes you'd recommend?
06:18 Samir Shah: Enable prefix caching for the top 50 intents, set batching target to 64 for embeddings jobs, enable server-side validation, and set retry policy to exponential backoff with jitter.
06:30 Maya Chen: I'll include config snippets in the follow-up.
06:34 Olivia Grant: One concern from infra: network egress costs when routing to eu-west — how do we estimate that?
06:40 Diego Rivera: We can provide a region-aware cost breakdown and an estimate of egress impact; usually egress is determined by your cloud provider, but routing within same region keeps it minimal.
06:50 Marcus Lee: Okay.
06:52 Maya Chen: Any blockers on the roadmap side? We plan to add improved model versioning, per-route caching controls and deeper quantization profiles in the next quarter. Does that align with your needs?
07:03 Olivia Grant: Yes. The per-route controls will be huge for us — we want different SLOs for embeddings vs chat.
07:10 Samir Shah: We'll surface that as a canary control so you can set route-level latency buckets.
07:16 Priya Nair: Security asks: can we use our HSM-backed KMS?
07:20 Maya Chen: Yes, we integrate with external KMS/HSM for Private deployments; for Dedicated we have options to bring your own key. I'll include the KMS integration guide.
07:30 Olivia Grant: Great.
07:34 Diego Rivera: Quick note — competitor question: have you evaluated Anthropic or OpenAI for the long docs?
07:39 Marcus Lee: We did some A/Bs, OpenAI was slightly better on coherence but cost was higher. We're leaning to optimize Redwood performance first.
07:48 Maya Chen: Okay — we'll include a short competitive note in the TCO.
07:52 Samir Shah: Next steps recap: Maya will send TCO and security docs by Oct 1; Marcus will send traffic sample by Oct 4; Samir will schedule the staging benchmark week of Oct 11; Diego will share traces link.
08:07 Olivia Grant: That works. Any other questions?
08:12 Priya Nair: One last ops question: what's the expected lead time to provision a dedicated pool?
08:17 Maya Chen: Typical lead time is 2-3 weeks for a small pool, less if you're flexible on exact GPU type. For Private deployments it's longer due to network setup.
08:26 Marcus Lee: OK. We'll aim to finalize commitment decision after pilot.
08:30 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc bundle.
08:34 Olivia Grant: Thanks all.
08:36 [meeting end]

Notes: transcript contains some ASR noise; speaker labels approximated. References shared: security pack https://redwood.in/security/soc2.pdf, qbr deck https://redwood.in/keystone/qbr-deck, traces link (private) https://redwood.app/keystone/traces/09-09
